statement: Blind annotation from the Beinecke scan alone (canvas '72v (part)' with two wheels; I describe the RIGHT-hand wheel, the one with a robed figure at the centre; a reduced view of the wheel and a full-resolution crop of its inner part). Identification of the panel is an inference, not a reading: f72v2 and f72v3 have the same label groups (18 and 12), so counts cannot separate them. I rely on the fold: on the recto canvas the panels run r1, r2, r3 away from the spine, so on the verso the back of r3 lies furthest left, and the wheel with the scales (identified as f72v1 by its inner count of 10) is the back of r1; the right-hand wheel of this canvas is then the back of r2. If that is wrong this annotation belongs to f72v3. Centre: a clothed figure in a blue-striped robe and blue hat holding a star. Two rings of nude standing figures without tubs, each with a star and a short label: 12 inner (counted on the scan), 18 outer (from the label group, not securely counted). Labels assigned from line ids and unit codes only, words not read; clockwise from the figure at the top by my assumption, so ids may be rotated by a constant within a ring. Ring figures carry generic features only.

features.position: centre
features.note: the only clothed figure on the wheel: a person in a long robe with blue vertical strokes and a blue rounded hat, a wide sleeve or cloak fanning out behind to the right with blue stripes, one hand held out to the left holding a star on a line; a small flower-like plant at the feet; a dark word in a different, Latin-like script to the left of the robe

features.position: centre, upper left of the figure
features.note: star joined by a line to the central figure's outstretched hand; no separate label seen
